title: Microsoft CEO Nadella Warns: If Retailers Block AI Shopping Agents, Market Share Could Flow to Open Platforms Like Shopify

content_html:
On November 18, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit that as software assistants increasingly take on product browsing and automatic ordering, retailers that refuse artificial intelligence shopping agents will risk losing customers, and their market share may be captured by more open competitors.

In his remarks, Nadella directly mentioned Amazon's current move to ban third-party AI agents from scanning its platform and completing orders on behalf of users, and noted that competing platforms such as Shopify only need to open checkout access to digital assistants to gain a significant competitive advantage.

He further argued that the spread of AI agents will not only change the e-commerce transaction chain, but also disrupt the traditional “human web” business model built on human visits and display advertising. As the primary browsing entity shifts from humans to bots, platforms that rely on sponsored listings, impulse purchases, and traditional traffic aggregation for profit will face structural reshaping, and future business models may need to shift toward pay-per-click or direct transaction settlement.

Nadella compared this evolution to the early internet's leap from portals such as Yahoo to Google search engines, arguing that every change in the traffic distribution mechanism redefines how commercial interests are distributed. Although the evolution of the competitive landscape between Amazon and Shopify is still at the prediction stage, as cross-web price comparison and automatic purchasing gradually become consumer habits, large retailers face an urgent strategic choice between protecting existing advertising revenue and adapting to the AI agent ecosystem.
